question: Should Browser CLI `--fields-file` accept a new fixed 1 MiB maximum, and if so what compatibility contract and user-facing documentation are required?
rationale: The current implementation deliberately rejects a class of inputs that the prior reader accepted; source and tests establish the mechanism but not the product limit.

options.title: Define and document a supported cap
options.body: Approve a justified limit, document the resulting error and upgrade behavior, and add boundary proof for existing valid usage.

options.title: Avoid a new fixed limit
options.body: Use a bounded or streaming strategy that prevents arbitrary buffering without rejecting previously accepted descriptor files at 1 MiB.

options.title: Pause for Browser CLI owner direction
options.body: Hold the PR until the Browser CLI input-size contract is decided by the relevant area owner.

recommendation.title: Define and document a supported cap
recommendation.body: Approve a justified limit, document the resulting error and upgrade behavior, and add boundary proof for existing valid usage.

likelyOwner.reason: A Browser CLI owner needs to decide whether rejecting formerly valid large descriptor files is an intended public contract.
